principles: Keep DONE merge semantics deterministic and observable.
Rebuild only when CLI runtime inputs changed so docs-only DONE remains fast.
Fail loudly on stale dist risk instead of silently reporting success.
Keep the implementation local to DONE merge effects and focused tests.
drivers: Global lattice points at packages/main/dist/cli.js in local development.
Missing build after DONE makes newly merged CLI commands unavailable.
The user asked for a hard rule rather than manual convention.

options.name: A: Rebuild packages/main after every DONE merge
pros: Eliminates stale dist after any DONE
cons: Adds unnecessary cost to docs-only or non-main-package stories
Could make unrelated DONE slower and noisier

options.name: B: Rebuild packages/main only when DONE merge changes CLI runtime inputs
pros: Can be covered with a deterministic changed-path predicate smoke
cons: Requires maintaining the watched path list
A missed runtime input path would skip build incorrectly

options.name: C: Add only a post-merge hook or documentation reminder
cons: Does not enforce the Lattice DONE path itself
Still relies on user environment and hook installation

chosen: B: Rebuild packages/main only when DONE merge changes CLI runtime inputs
rationale: Choose a targeted hard rule in applyDoneMergeEffects: compare main before/after merge, rebuild packages/main when source/package runtime inputs changed, and surface build failure explicitly. This fixes the stale global lattice problem without turning every DONE into an unconditional build.

preMortem.scenario: Changed-path list misses a real CLI runtime input
preMortem.trigger: A story edits a runtime-affecting file outside the watched prefixes
preMortem.consequence: DONE skips build and global lattice stays stale
preMortem.mitigation: Use conservative watched prefixes: packages/main/src, packages/main/package.json, packages/main/tsconfig.json, root package.json, and package-lock.json; add smoke coverage for representative paths.

preMortem.scenario: Post-merge build failure leaves DONE looking successful
preMortem.trigger: TypeScript compile fails after the story branch has already merged to main
preMortem.consequence: User believes DONE completed while dist is stale
preMortem.mitigation: Throw a clear post-merge rebuild error with command/output/recovery guidance before cleanup/reporting completes.

preMortem.scenario: Smoke test becomes slow or brittle by running a full real DONE merge with npm build
preMortem.trigger: Test shells out through the entire lifecycle and package manager
preMortem.consequence: Local validation becomes expensive and flaky
preMortem.mitigation: Expose small helper functions for changed-path detection/build execution and cover them with task-level smoke, while existing DONE merge smoke continues to cover integration shape.
